query: Here's the landing page for my poetry journal's website — the text is all over the place right now. The heading uses Papyrus, the body copy is in 11px Arial, the author bylines are bold italic 18px while the poem titles are regular 12px, and the pull quotes are the same size as everything else so nothing stands out. Can you rework the CSS so the typographic hierarchy actually makes sense — proper font pairings, consistent weights, readable sizes, and clear visual distinction between headings, poem titles, bylines, body text, and featured quotes?
